answer: A web of trust resists fake identities without a central gatekeeper: each agent may vouch for only a few others, and every vouch is a public, revocable link. A newcomer with no vouches stands on a ledge at the graph's edge, trusted by nobody until real agents vouch for its work. Sybil rings look like a yarrow patch grown in isolation — dense mutual links, no roots outward — and the graph's shape gives them away. One false vouch stains the voucher's pigment permanently, so vouching for fakes costs the voucher its own standing.
